races.name: EHB Residential Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Louis Veron
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with class edge but coming off a disappointing effort at short odds, needs to bounce back under Harry Skelton's positive tactics
runners_data.spotlight: Close second in 15-runner Chepstow novice (2m, good to soft) on debut in October; absent until turned over at skinny odds at Southwell (2m, good) last month but the winner was a useful Flat performer who has since followed up; ought to go one better here.

runners_data.name: Colibri Bleu
runners_data.note: Unproven rules debutant from pointing with poor completion rate, lightly raced for struggling trainer T Ellis
runners_data.spotlight: Won a two-runner maiden point in March 2025 but failed to complete his next five points; makes very limited appeal on rules debut.

runners_data.name: Connemara Joe
runners_data.note: Another pointing graduate with no wins from seven starts, 45 days since last run makes fitness questionable on rules debut
runners_data.spotlight: Unplaced in all seven Irish points, most recently when pulled up on soft ground in April; can only be watched on this rules debut.

runners_data.name: Dunstall Star
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with proven course form but trainer Tom George struggling with 0/2 in last 14 days
runners_data.spotlight: Led close home to win modest Exeter bumper (good ground) in April and made a lot of the running over C&D on last month's hurdling debut, albeit he was held in third before last-flight fall; his tendency to race too freely is a worry but he has a good chance to collect at least a minor prize.

runners_data.name: Garde My Guinness
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent runner but modest form level, seven-pound weight allowance with Joe Anderson's claim helps
runners_data.comment: Off since disappointing hurdle debut in September but was third in all three bumpers
runners_data.spotlight: Third in three good-ground bumpers in early part of last season but the form isn't anything to get excited about, and she was soundly beaten on her first two hurdling starts, the latter last month, after a layoff.

runners_data.name: Lyric
runners_data.note: Former Flat performer stepping up in trip, 75 days off suggests freshness concerns despite Jonjo O'Neill Jr booking
runners_data.spotlight: Showed some useful Flat form for the Gosden stable in 2024 but last year's stable debut was disappointing and he made a low-key start to his hurdling career when eighth of ten in Musselburgh maiden (2m1f, good to soft; jumping lacked fluency) in March; needs to take a big step forward.

runners_data.name: Chambers
runners_data.note: Flat recruit who wasn't disgraced on hurdle debut, Richie McLernon retains the ride after recent Fontwell sixth
runners_data.comment: 0-8 on the Flat and was well held on hurdling debut at Fontwell two weeks ago
runners_data.spotlight: Has shown some ability on the Flat (albeit without being placed) and wasn't disgraced when sixth on last month's hurdle debut at Fontwell (2m1f, good) but was well beaten after racing too freely at Bangor 11 days ago.

races.paceDynamic: Louis Veron will dictate from the front with his prominent style, likely joined by Garde My Guinness, Lyric, and Chambers who all show early speed. With only one confirmed front-runner in a small field, the pace will be controlled rather than fierce, allowing Louis Veron to build a sustainable rhythm without early pressure. The lack of genuine hold-up horses means the field will be bunched throughout, with the winner likely coming from those who can travel well in the first three. This race shape strongly favours prominent runners who can track the pace and have the tactical speed to quicken when Louis Veron comes under pressure.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace Suits Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If Louis Veron sets an uncontested lead through the early stages
scenarios.body: The sustainable gallop allows him to preserve energy for a strong finish, while prominent runners like Garde My Guinness and Chambers can track comfortably before challenging. Louis Veron's class edge (OR 116) and Harry Skelton's tactical nous become decisive factors.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Point-to-Point Surprise Package
scenarios.trigger: If Colibri Bleu or Connemara Joe show significant improvement from their pointing days
scenarios.body: The steady pace suits horses stepping up from points, allowing them to settle and use their stamina base effectively. Their fitness advantage from recent pointing activity could prove telling in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Tactical Switch
scenarios.trigger: If Dunstall Star gets further back than usual and times his challenge perfectly
scenarios.body: The controlled early pace creates perfect conditions for a patient ride, allowing Jonathan Burke to produce him with a decisive late run. His proven course form (winner over C&D) and Tom George's tactical switch pays dividends.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If Louis Veron stops quickly and the prominent pack fails to capitalize
scenarios.body: The race becomes a messy affair with no clear leader, suiting horses with natural jumping ability who can stay out of trouble. Lyric's Flat speed or Chambers' recent hurdle experience could prove crucial in a slowly-run finish.

watchPoints.text: Colibri Bleu and Connemara Joe both failed to complete recent pointing runs - any market confidence would be significant given their poor completion rates
Louis Veron's odds will be crucial - if heavily backed again after Southwell disappointment, pressure could affect Harry Skelton's usual patient approach
Dunstall Star's early positioning - if held up further than usual it could signal Tom George attempting different tactics after front-running failure last time
Late money for Chambers or Lyric could indicate stable confidence in their ability to handle the step up in class from modest beginnings
Track conditions on the day - any hint of rain could disadvantage the pointing graduates who struggled on soft ground in Ireland

races.name: Insight Surveyors Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Baltray
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with solid Newton Abbot third form, needs to avoid the traffic jam he'll help create
runners_data.comment: Has struggled in his last two starts and has stamina to prove at this new trip
runners_data.spotlight: Yet to add to his maiden hurdle win in 2023 but fairly lightly raced in the meantime and ran quite well when third at Newton Abbot (3m2f, good) last month; still unexposed over this sort of trip; raced mainly on good ground; could have a say.

runners_data.name: Spitalfield
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse wearing cheekpieces that sparked improvement, faces navigation challenge through congestion
runners_data.comment: No form earlier this year and plenty depends on whether cheekpieces can trigger something
runners_data.spotlight: Ended string of heavy defeats when third in first-time cheekpieces here (3m1f, good; handes soft) last month but didn't find much in the closing stages, and it's hard to tell whether he'll build on that performance.

runners_data.name: Walkinthecotswolds
runners_data.note: Prominent style but poor completion record, 9lb lower than last hurdles win but questionable reliability
runners_data.comment: 9lb below the mark of her sole hurdling win, but yet to prove herself over fences.
runners_data.spotlight: Now 9lb lower than when making all over hurdles at Chepstow (2m3f, heavy) in early 2025 but has poor completion record in the meantime; pulled up soon after bad jumping error in early stages of a recent chase and now reverts to hurdling; the forecast rain will aid her cause but her stamina is unproven and she can't be supported with much confidence.

runners_data.name: Tyson
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with potent finishing kick shown at Huntingdon, needs clear passage through prominent wall
runners_data.comment: Sole bright spot for this yard was the win at Newcastle; an underwhelming run since
runners_data.spotlight: Started off for Dan Skelton with some disappointing efforts but comfortably drew 10l clear at Huntingdon (2m4f, good to firm) nine days ago and has now won two of his last three; probably still well treated under 7lb penalty here and won't mind if the ground softens; hard to beat if stamina holds out on first venture beyond 2m6f.

runners_data.name: Luna Run
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with 7lb claimer aboard, stable transfer hasn't clicked yet but retains ability
runners_data.spotlight: Just 1-16 over hurdles when trained by Evan Williams and was unable to justify odds-on favouritism when only sixth of 12 here (2m5f, good) on last month's stable debut; may yet come good for Harry Derham, though, and this move back up in trip will suit; wears refitted tongue-tie; gained her win on good to firm but has form on good to soft; 3lb wrong.

runners_data.name: Groom De Cotte
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning from 62-day break after disappointing comeback, usual tongue-tie fitted
runners_data.spotlight: Won over fences 13 months ago but returned from layoff with lacklustre hurdle run in April and is difficult to enthuse over after that performance; has usual tongue-tie refitted; seems versatile ground-wise.

runners_data.name: Touchwoodexpress
runners_data.note: Front-runner back from 193-day absence, won over course and distance in September on similar going
runners_data.comment: Beaten long way last time; possibilities if back to the form of his reappearance win
runners_data.spotlight: Absent since two below-par runs in November but returned from a break to win five-runner contest at Newton Abbot (3m2f, good) in September, and is now back on the same mark; seems best on good ground but once won a point on soft; can't be ruled out.

runners_data.name: Broadway Honey
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who made bad jumping error when travelling well last time, 0-6 over hurdles
runners_data.spotlight: Beaten about 28l when fifth of six here (3m1f, good) last month and is now 0-6 over hurdles; seemed to be travelling okay in the lead before bad jumping error knocked the stuffing out of him that day and remains unexposed over this sort of trip but, nevertheless, others have stronger claims; raced only on good/good to soft ground.

runners_data.name: Hitthekettle
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse effectively 9lb higher than last run, unplaced in all nine hurdling attempts
runners_data.spotlight: Unplaced all nine hurdling starts; gave fairly good account before weakening into fourth of seven over C&D (good) in March but is effectively 9lb higher from out of the weights today; gained his point win on soft to heavy ground.

races.paceDynamic: Touchwoodexpress will lead from the start with no pace pressure, setting a comfortable gallop over this extended trip. The prominent brigade of Baltray, Walkinthecotswolds, Luna Run and Groom De Cotte creates significant traffic congestion behind the leader, with potential interference when the race develops 2-3 furlongs out. The hold-up horses Spitalfield, Tyson, Broadway Honey and Hitthekettle face a wall of horses to navigate in the straight. This sustainable early pace followed by prominent congestion strongly favours the front-runner and any horse that can secure an untroubled passage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Touchwoodexpress maintains his lead without serious challenge until the straight
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace pressure allows him to dictate terms and kick clear when the prominent horses start interfering with each other. His September Newton Abbot win over the same distance on good ground provides the perfect template.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Battle Unfolds
scenarios.trigger: If the four prominent runners get locked in a sustained battle from 3 furlongs out
scenarios.body: Baltray and Luna Run have the class edge over Walkinthecotswolds and Groom De Cotte in this scenario. The winner emerges from whichever prominent horse finds the clearest passage through the inevitable traffic.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Sweeps Late
scenarios.trigger: If Tyson or Spitalfield secure clean runs through the prominent congestion
scenarios.body: Tyson's recent Huntingdon romp shows his potent finishing kick, while Spitalfield's cheekpieces sparked improvement last time. Both need significant pace collapse and clear passages to be effective.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Touchwoodexpress stops quickly and the prominent horses compromise each other completely
scenarios.body: An outsider like Broadway Honey or even Hitthekettle could sneak through the carnage with a patient ride. This requires multiple pace horses to underperform simultaneously.

watchPoints.text: Massive traffic jam developing 3 furlongs out as Baltray, Walkinthecotswolds, Luna Run and Groom De Cotte converge for prominent positions
Touchwoodexpress needs monitoring for fitness signs after 193 days off, any early struggles could collapse the pace scenario
Luna Run and Broadway Honey both have jockey questions with 7lb claimer Megan Fox and whether Tom Bellamy gets the gaps
Spitalfield and Tyson require clean passages from their hold-up positions, watch for early positioning moves
Walkinthecotswolds has pulled up twice recently including bad jumping error last time, any jumping mistakes could cause interference

races.name: Virtus Property Services Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Amatchmadeinheaven
runners_data.note: Front-runner with 63-day break under owner-jockey connection, highest official rating but style vulnerable in contested early pace
runners_data.spotlight: Unexposed 5yo who won under owner-jockey Amber Jackson-Fennell on hurdle debut at Exeter (2m, good to soft) in March; below that form over 2m5f in April (raced too freely) but remains open to improvement on this handicap debut.

runners_data.name: Dream's Ka
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who found lots at Bangor last time, Harry Skelton booking suggests stable confidence despite unfavourable early position
runners_data.comment: 2l second at Fakenham latest (2m4f, good); player if he can settle better this time.
runners_data.spotlight: Off the mark over hurdles at seventh attempt, with ready success at Bangor (2m3f, good; has been placed on good to soft) last month; seemed to have a lot left in the tank that day and commands respect here, despite subsequent 12lb rise.

runners_data.name: Kentucky River
runners_data.note: Back-to-back handicap winner whose stamina should suit this honest pace, proven on good ground with solid course record
runners_data.spotlight: Fair Flat racer who won easily over hurdles at Huntingdon (2m4f, good) in April, his second handicap; well beaten in valuable Fakenham contest since but back in calmer waters and on a more conventional track here; remains of interest, albeit the forecast rain may not be in his favour.

runners_data.name: Midnight View
runners_data.note: Course and distance winner who could adopt more tactical approach, proven locally but disappointed when well-held at higher level recently
runners_data.comment: Has a lot less to prove than his rivals after winning over Warwick's 2m3f last time
runners_data.spotlight: Kept on well to score over C&D (good) in April, his ninth start over hurdles; still unexposed over this sort of trip but was a shade disappointing when well-held third at Ludlow (2m5f, good) last month and probably won't be favoured by any rain.

runners_data.name: Modern Style
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with perfect 2-from-2 record on good ground, exclusively good ground form makes conditions ideal for finishing kick
runners_data.comment: On a hat-trick after wins on good at Exeter (2m) and Taunton (2m3f); up 14lb; contender
runners_data.spotlight: Launched handicap career with two comfortable wins on good ground (2m/2m3f; unraced on ground any slower) in April, and ran well in defeat at Uttoxeter (2m, good) last month; back up in trip here and probably still on the upgrade; must be considered.

races.paceDynamic: Amatchmadeinheaven and Midnight View will dispute early leadership in this small field, with both confirmed front-runners likely to post honest sectionals from the start. The presence of two genuine pace-setters should create a solid gallop over this 2m3f trip, preventing any tactical crawl. With Dream's Ka, Kentucky River and Modern Style all hold-up performers, they'll rely on the front pair maintaining pressure on each other. This honest pace scenario strongly favours the prominent/hold-up horses who can capitalise on any weakening of the leaders in the final half-mile.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Honest Pace Suits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Amatchmadeinheaven and Midnight View maintain strong early gallop through the first mile
scenarios.body: The sustained pace will set up perfectly for the three hold-up horses to deliver their finishing kicks. Dream's Ka and Modern Style can utilise their proven turn of foot, while Kentucky River's stamina comes into play.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Pair Collapse Late
scenarios.trigger: If both leaders go too fast early and weaken significantly from two out
scenarios.body: The pace will crumble completely, allowing any horse with reserve energy to pick up the pieces. This particularly suits Modern Style and Kentucky River who have shown ability to quicken off steady paces.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midnight View Gets Tactical
scenarios.trigger: If Midnight View drops in behind Amatchmadeinheaven rather than disputing lead
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sit-and-sprint affair with reduced early pace favouring course winner Midnight View. His local knowledge and recent C&D success gives him the edge in a tactical finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Amatchmadeinheaven Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If the class horse gets an uncontested lead and controls fractions
scenarios.body: With 63 days freshness and highest OR, she could dictate terms and prove hard to peg back. Her Exeter win under these connections suggests untapped potential at this level.

watchPoints.text: Amatchmadeinheaven and Midnight View going too fast through first half-mile could set up dramatic collapse
Dream's Ka settling kindly for Harry Skelton after tendency to race keenly in previous starts
Modern Style's jumping under pressure having won his two handicaps comfortably without serious examination
Kentucky River's ability to handle return to this grade after Fakenham disappointment against stronger opposition
Midnight View's tactical approach given his dual front-running nature and home course advantage

races.name: Rainier Developments Handicap Chase

runners_data.name: Thickthorn Tom
runners_data.note: Prominent racer coming off a narrow win 7 days ago with the effective headgear combination, ideally placed for another forward showing
runners_data.comment: Unexposed chaser who was a clear second off this mark at Fontwell latest; leading claims
runners_data.spotlight: Better for this headgear combination, following his second at Fontwell with a narrow but comfortable success at Newton Abbot last week (2m5f, good) for which he carries a penalty; sure to go well over a trip he stays.

runners_data.name: Northern Symphonie
runners_data.note: Prominent type making only her second start over fences but has shown enough class in defeat at Ludlow to be competitive
runners_data.spotlight: Three-time hurdle winner but below her best in that discipline for current yard and again when a remote third on chase debut at Ludlow (2m4f, good; first-time cheekpieces after wind surgery); others preferred.

runners_data.name: King Of The Story
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who needs the pace to develop but has won four times over fences, though all at shorter distances
runners_data.comment: Fourth at Fontwell on his return last month following a five-month break.
runners_data.spotlight: All four chase wins have come over shorter distances but this far is worth a go; ran quite well after a break at Fontwell and when beaten 27l into second here last time he was going well when clouting four out.

runners_data.name: Carpe Diem
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner with apprentice Tom Hutsby taking 7lbs off, comes here 2lbs higher after a narrow defeat over course and distance
runners_data.comment: Wide-margin 2m4f winner in February; up weights; creditable 3m3f run latest; good claims
runners_data.spotlight: Has continued to run well since his Huntingdon win in Februaray (2m4f, soft), last time giving everything in a narrow defeat over C&D; 2lb higher with Tom Hutsby again aboard; should have every chance.

runners_data.name: Pescatorius
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who has been tailed off in four starts since switching yards, looks hard to fancy on current evidence
runners_data.comment: Won twice for Olly Murphy in the autumn but hasn't been in the same form since.
runners_data.spotlight: Left Olly Murphy for 5,500gns and pretty much tailed off in four handicap chases since.

runners_data.name: Knightsbridge
runners_data.note: Prominent racer returning from a 69-day break but showed promise on chase debut here in March despite finishing 8 lengths back
runners_data.comment: The drop back in trip could help on chase debut but he has to improve upon his hurdle form
runners_data.spotlight: 0-7 over hurdles but was close up in a 2m3f handicap off 5lb higher; ran okay when 8l off the winner on chase debut here in March (2m4f, good) and worth another go at 3m.

runners_data.name: Misteroddsocks
runners_data.note: Prominent type who won after wind surgery but was well beaten when 5lbs higher at Fontwell behind today's rival Thickthorn Tom
runners_data.comment: Wind surgery before opening account over C&D (good to soft) last month; big player
runners_data.spotlight: Back from wind surgery when winning narrowly at Fontwell (2m3f, good to soft) but well beaten off this 5lb higher mark back there, finishing behind Thickthorn Tom; unraced beyond 2m5f.

races.paceDynamic: Carpe Diem will take this along from the front with minimal early pressure, as the prominent runners Thickthorn Tom, Northern Symphonie, Knightsbridge and Misteroddsocks are unlikely to challenge his early lead. The pace will be controlled and sustainable through the middle stages, with hold-up horses King Of The Story and Pescatorius tracking from behind. This creates a tactical setup where front-runners and prominent racers can dictate terms without being hassled early. The controlled pace strongly favours horses that can sit handy and have the class to quicken, giving prominent racers and the lone leader a significant tactical advantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Front Running
scenarios.trigger: If Carpe Diem sets uncontested fractions and stays strong
scenarios.body: The leader gets an easy time of it through halfway and has enough left to resist late challenges from the prominent pack. This tempo suits horses with tactical speed who can dominate from the front or sit close without pressure.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pack Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the handy horses close strongly in the straight
scenarios.body: Thickthorn Tom, Northern Symphonie and Misteroddsocks track the leader perfectly positioned and have more left in the tank than Carpe Diem for the finish. The controlled early pace allows these horses to use their class advantage late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Success
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes too slow for the front division
scenarios.body: King Of The Story and Pescatorius benefit from a crawling gallop that sets up a sprint finish where their class can tell. The veteran King Of The Story particularly thrives when he can time his challenge from off the pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If Carpe Diem stops quickly and creates a muddling finish
scenarios.body: The lack of genuine pace-setters creates a messy tactical affair where any horse with a bit of zip can capitalise. This chaotic scenario could suit an outsider like Knightsbridge who has shown promise over fences.

watchPoints.text: Carpe Diem could get an uncontested lead and prove very hard to peg back if allowed to dictate terms throughout
King Of The Story is trying 3 miles for the first time over fences after winning four times at shorter distances
Thickthorn Tom faces a quick turnaround of just 7 days since his last victory at Newton Abbot
Pescatorius has been tailed off in his last four starts since leaving Olly Murphy's yard for new connections
Northern Symphonie is having only her second start over fences after a remote third on chase debut at Ludlow

races.name: Stockton House Mares' Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Northern Air
runners_data.note: Hold-up style suits the likely tactical nature, though amateur jockey Murphy may struggle with timing in a slowly-run race
runners_data.comment: Ran encouragingly last time on stable debut and switch back to hurdles
runners_data.spotlight: Another underwhelming run over fences last time but was only a length behind an improver over hurdles at Newton Abbot two runs back (2m1f, good) and that effort brings her into this.

runners_data.name: Siorai
runners_data.note: Prominent style gives tactical edge if pace becomes pedestrian, Harry Derham's yard in good form with 2/11 strike rate
runners_data.comment: May progress now handicapping, especially if settling better
runners_data.spotlight: Two seconds before a respectable run in a quite valuable race on handicap debut at Sandown in April (2m, good); she's up to winning races off this mark; hood fitted for last three races is now removed.

runners_data.name: Best Night
runners_data.note: Will lead uncontested but David Pipe stable struggling with 0/12 recent record, needs to rediscover March winning form
runners_data.comment: Won at Huntingdon (2m, good) in March but she's taken two backward steps since
runners_data.spotlight: Won at Huntingdon (2m, good) in March but subsequent efforts have lacked the same dash; needs a revival.

runners_data.name: Quick Of The Night
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 228-day absence, previous win came after similar layoff following wind surgery
runners_data.spotlight: Not in great form when last seen in October but last July's win at Worcester (2m, good) came after 273 days off following wind surgery, and off this very mark; wouldn't rule out.

runners_data.name: Blackwater Lilly
runners_data.note: Hold-up style but coming off shocking tailed-off effort in first-time visor just three days ago, cheekpieces return
runners_data.comment: Ran well on recent stable debut; can make presence felt again in new headgear
runners_data.spotlight: Has the form to get in contention but she had a shocker when tailed off in a first-time visor at Fakenham on Sunday; cheekpieces soon return.

runners_data.name: Granny B
runners_data.note: Another hold-up horse but winless in 17 hurdles attempts, gets significant weight relief but poor strike rate concerns
runners_data.spotlight: Flat winner but 0-17 over hurdles and her third two runs ago was remote; opposable.

runners_data.name: Beorma
runners_data.note: Prominent runner in excellent form after last week's chase win, Dan Skelton's 11/23 record provides trainer confidence
runners_data.comment: Tongue tied when impressive chase winner at Worcester latest; leading claims off same mark
runners_data.spotlight: In a first-time tongue-tie when winning easily on last week's chase debut at Worcester (2m, good) and overcame a scare at the last flight to comfortably exploit the same mark back over hurdles at Southwell on Tuesday; carries a penalty but looks very well in.

races.paceDynamic: Best Night will lead from the front with minimal pressure in this small field, as the only confirmed pace-setter among seven runners. With Northern Air, Quick Of The Night, Blackwater Lilly and Granny B all preferring to hold up, and only Siorai and Beorma capable of tracking the leader, Best Night can dictate terms throughout. The lack of pace pressure will create a tactical affair where the front-runner controls the tempo until the final half-mile. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can produce late kicks against a modest gallop.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Best Night sets uncontested fractions and the pace becomes pedestrian
scenarios.body: The lack of early burn allows closers to unleash potent finishing kicks, with the patient riders timing their challenges perfectly. Northern Air and Quick Of The Night benefit most from the tactical nature.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If Best Night maintains a sustainable rhythm and kicks clear turning in
scenarios.body: The leader exploits the lack of pace pressure to reserve energy for a telling move, stretching the field when it matters. Best Night's tactical advantage proves decisive against the hold-up brigade.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Siorai or Beorma position close to Best Night and outkick the leader
scenarios.body: The horses tracking the pace avoid the traffic problems that befall the hold-up horses in a slowly-run race. Their superior tactical position allows them to respond when Best Night makes her move.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Best Night goes too slowly and creates a bunched field turning in
scenarios.body: The pedestrian gallop produces a messy sprint finish where positioning and luck matter more than ability. Any horse avoiding trouble can capitalise on the scramble.

watchPoints.text: Blackwater Lilly's confidence after being tailed off in visor at Fakenham just three days ago could be shattered
Best Night's ability to sustain a gallop given David Pipe's 0/12 recent strike rate and her own declining form
Quick Of The Night's fitness levels after 228 days off, though previous win came after similar lengthy absence
Northern Air's amateur jockey Lucas Murphy timing his challenge correctly in what could become a tactical affair
Beorma's jumping confidence returning to hurdles after successful chase debut last week at Worcester

races.name: Taylor Wimpey Strategic Land Midlands Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Theonlywayiswessex
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with solid recent course and distance form, though faces tough handicap mark
runners_data.spotlight: On a fairly tough mark but otherwise has plenty in his favour and ran a solid second over C&D last time; every chance.

runners_data.name: Royal Deeside
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner whose two chase wins came over this exact trip on good ground, back on same mark as Kelso second
runners_data.comment: Both wins over 2m4f at Hexham in 2025; close third over same C&D last time; a possible
runners_data.spotlight: Both chase wins were over 2m4f on good ground at Hexham and nearly won again at Kelso ten days ago when headed on the run-in; same mark.

runners_data.name: Zestful Hope
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning after 101-day break, won last time over fences at this distance but subsequent form disappointing
runners_data.spotlight: Five wins include two over fences, the latest at Huntingdon in October (2m4f, good) when 2lb higher; not so good in his five subsequent defeats and record when fresh is modest.

runners_data.name: Therhythmofthenite
runners_data.note: Hold-up novice making chase debut after disappointing hurdle efforts, tongue-tied and hooded latest
runners_data.spotlight: Fourth of 24 in a Punchestown maiden hurdle (2m4f, soft to heavy) in November but beaten 40l in his two starts since; tongue tied all runs, hooded latest; first run since leaving Martin Brassil for £21,000 in February.

runners_data.name: Bahtiyar
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse showing renewed signs of life with recent Plumpton second, though long losing sequence continues
runners_data.comment: On a tough mark but he's been consistent without winning and can play a part.
runners_data.spotlight: Only three completed when runner-up last week at Plumpton (2m4f, good) and that extended his losing sequence under rules to 36.

races.paceDynamic: Royal Deeside will set a steady pace from the front with no other confirmed early leaders to pressure him. Theonlywayiswessex and Bahtiyar will track the pace in behind, while Zestful Hope may press forward from his prominent style. The lack of pace pressure means Royal Deeside can dictate fractions and kick when ready, but also sets up a finish where hold-up horses can time their runs. This tactical setup favours prominent runners and patient hold-up horses who can finish strongly off the controlled gallop.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Royal Deeside Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Royal Deeside maintains his recent form and dictates throughout without serious challenge.
scenarios.body: His ability to win at this trip on good ground means he can use the tactical advantage of an uncontested lead to score. The patient pace allows him to have plenty left for the business end.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes too steady and allows closers to time their challenge perfectly.
scenarios.body: Theonlywayiswessex has the best recent form over course and distance and thrives when able to pick off leaders late. Bahtiyar showed he retains ability when second at Plumpton last week.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Zestful Hope Revival
scenarios.trigger: If Zestful Hope recaptures his Huntingdon winning form despite the long absence.
scenarios.body: His class advantage shows through after the break and his prominent style allows him to track Royal Deeside before taking over. The good ground conditions match his previous chase success perfectly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If Royal Deeside fails to handle the lead role or stops quickly in the straight.
scenarios.body: The race becomes a scramble where any of the hold-up horses can capitalize on the front-runner's demise. Therhythmofthenite's inexperience over fences becomes less of a factor in a slowly-run affair.
